items.content: The moment you cross the threshold, it reaches you — that particular perfume of decades, a warm musk of yellowing paper and binding glue, of dust settled so long it has become something almost sacred. It is the smell of unread afternoons, of marginalia written by hands long still, of stories waiting with the patience of stones. Something in it pulls at a memory you cannot quite locate, older perhaps than yourself, as though the books are exhaling all the hours they have quietly kept.

items.content: The coffee had been brewing since before anyone woke, its dark ribbon of steam curling upward through the blue half-light like something trying to remember warmth. She stood in the doorway in bare feet, not yet ready to speak or be spoken to, letting the smell reach her first — bitter and familiar, older somehow than the morning itself. The kitchen held its silence the way kitchens do at that hour, when the house still belongs to no one.

items.content: The ceiling was wrong — too white, too still, with a water stain shaped like nothing she recognized. She lay motionless for a moment, listening to the hum of an air conditioner that belonged to no home she had ever known, watching thin bars of light press through curtains the color of old mustard. The room assembled itself slowly around her: a suitcase half-open like a wound, a keycard on the nightstand, the faint ghost of someone else's cologne in the sheets. She was somewhere, at least. That much was certain.
